speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the vertigo you are experiencing? Specifically, does the room feel like it is spinning around you, or do you feel unsteady and lightheaded?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since the episode was brief and you are currently feeling at your baseline, I need to check for any associated neurological symptoms. Did you experience any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or difficulty speaking or walking during the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of ear problems, such as frequent ear infections or tinnitus, and does the vertigo seem to be triggered by specific changes in head position?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient is otherwise healthy with only a history of eczema. No prior episodes of similar nature. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the episode lasted only three minutes and was triggered by going to bed, I suspect a positional issue. Does the vertigo recur if you turn your head to the left or right, or look up?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headaches, hearing loss, tinnitus, loss of consciousness or neurological deficits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of hearing loss, tinnitus, and neurological deficits, combined with the brief, position-triggered nature of the episode, strongly points to Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this clinical suspicion and rule out other vestibular causes, I will now perform a physical examination.

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Maneuver
